slides.title: cpdef vs cdef vs def in Cython
slides.prompt: What distinguishes a `cpdef` function declaration in Cython from `cdef` or standard `def`?
options: It generates both a fast C-level entry point and a Python-compatible wrapper function
It forces the function to execute on remote GPU clusters
It disables type checking entirely at compile time
It restricts function execution to C++ source compilers
slides.correctAnswer: It generates both a fast C-level entry point and a Python-compatible wrapper function

slides.title: Ctypes vs CFFI vs Cython
slides.prompt: Why choose CFFI (C Foreign Function Interface) or Cython over standard `ctypes` for high-throughput libraries?
options: They provide C-compile-time performance validation and avoid dynamic `ctypes` marshaling runtime overhead
They eliminate the need for a C compiler during build steps
They automatically translate Python code to Rust
They remove Linux operating system kernel boundaries
slides.correctAnswer: They provide C-compile-time performance validation and avoid dynamic `ctypes` marshaling runtime overhead

slides.title: Bounds Checking Disabling Compiler Directives
slides.prompt: What trade-off is made when applying `@cython.boundscheck(False)` to a Cython array processing loop?
options: It removes array index boundary safety checks for max execution speed, but risks memory segfaults on out-of-bounds access
It converts integer arrays into floating-point vectors
It automatically parallelizes loop steps across CPU sockets
It encrypts array memory buffers in RAM
slides.correctAnswer: It removes array index boundary safety checks for max execution speed, but risks memory segfaults on out-of-bounds access
